Four primary-source pages, one internal link back to this curriculum's Part 11 depth, and six further resources (video, guidance, and tools). All
four eCFR links were curl-verified (`curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -L <url>`) and
returned `200` at the time this page was written.

- **[45 CFR 164.306, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.306)**
  — the general rules section this module leans on hardest: the overall confidentiality/integrity/
  availability mandate in (a), and the Required-vs-Addressable mechanism in (d) that this whole
  module turns on.

- **[45 CFR 164.308, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.308)**
  — the administrative safeguards: risk analysis, workforce security, security incident
  procedures, and the information-system-activity-review requirement behind this module's
  verification-gap finding.

- **[45 CFR 164.310, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.310)**
  — the physical safeguards, including device and media controls, the standard most directly on
  point for a laptop carrying e-PHI (electronic protected health information) leaving a facility.

- **[45 CFR 164.312, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.312)**
  — the technical safeguards: access control (including the Required unique-user-ID specification
  and the Addressable encryption specification the laptop's status turns on), audit controls, and
  person/entity authentication.

- **[`audit-trails-and-esignatures`, this curriculum](../../data-integrity-and-records/audit-trails-and-esignatures/index.qmd)**
  — where 21 CFR Part 11's own audit-trail (11.10(e)), signature (11.50, 11.70), identity
  (11.100), execution (11.200), and credential-control (11.300) requirements are quoted and
  taught in full. Read it if you want the complete Part 11 text behind the comparison table above
  — none of it is re-quoted at length in this module.

- **[HHS OCR - HIPAA Security Rule](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QWRn2r5R7ts)** (USGovHHSOCR,
  from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson, from the HIPAA regulator's own
  YouTube channel. A general overview of the Security Rule, not specific to blood establishments or
  Part 11. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2: Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/66/r2/final)**
  — NIST's cybersecurity resource guide mapping each Security Rule standard to practical
  implementation steps. Read it when you want to see how a control such as encryption or activity
  review is actually put into practice. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures — Scope and Application](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/part-11-electronic-records-electronic-signatures-scope-and-application)**
  — FDA's guidance page on how it applies Part 11, including its enforcement-discretion approach.
  Read it for the Part 11 side of this lesson's comparison. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR Part 11](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/part-11)** — a
  readable mirror of the full Part 11 text, for checking the sections the comparison table
  references. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[eCFR: 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C (Security Standards)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C)**
  — the whole Security Rule subpart on one page, including 164.314 and 164.316, which this lesson
  names but does not quote. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[HealthIT.gov: Security Risk Assessment Tool](https://www.healthit.gov/topic/privacy-security-and-hipaa/security-risk-assessment-tool)**
  — the federal tool page for the 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) risk analysis this lesson says an
  investigator would ask for first. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about the HIPAA Security Rule, risk analysis, and encryption.

- **[HIPAA Security Rule](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-security-rule/)** (HIPAA Journal) — a clear tour of the administrative, physical and technical safeguards and the required-versus-addressable idea. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[What are the HIPAA Technical Safeguards?](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-technical-safeguards/)** (HIPAA Journal) — focuses on access control, audit controls, integrity and transmission security, the part closest to an IT operations role. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[HIPAA Encryption Requirements](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-encryption-requirements/)** (HIPAA Journal) — a practitioner explainer on how encryption is treated, helpful context for the lesson's addressable-control question. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[The HIPAA Risk Analysis: Guidance and Tools](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-risk-analysis/)** (HIPAA Journal) — how organizations structure a risk analysis, with tool pointers. Supports CISSP Domain 1 (risk management concepts). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cybersecurity Posters and Cheat Sheets](https://www.sans.org/security-resources/posters/)** (SANS Institute) — free one-page references on controls, logging and defensive practice; handy for CISSP Domain 3 and Domain 7 review. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
